oracle.description: templates/dispatch/tests/test_release_scorecard_entrypoint.py decides correctness, and it drives the script through subprocess rather than importing it. That is the entire point: T-6d shipped 31 green tests over main(argv) called in process, and the file still did nothing at all when run as a command.

purpose: Make templates/dispatch/scripts/release_scorecard.py runnable as a command, and make a wrong invocation fail loudly. Change nothing else. First, add a __main__ entry point so that running the file as a program executes main and exits with its return value. Today there is none, so the command exits 0 and writes nothing -- the row this implements says a scorecard is produced by running a command, and the existing tests all graded a function called in process. Second, --release, --sink, --receipts and --out are required: invoked without any one of them the command must exit non-zero, write something to stderr, and leave no output file behind. An implementation that errors after writing has still corrupted the evidence directory, so the ordering matters. Today a missing flag silently yields a scorecard whose release is null, which is worse than failing, because a scorecard that names no release gets filed against the wrong one. An unknown flag must also exit non-zero rather than being silently ignored. Third, --help must exit 0 and name the flags. The optional flags stay optional: a run with no --escalations, no --since and no --until succeeds and reports an escalations count of zero. Everything already settled stays exactly as it is -- the six computation functions, and main's behaviour for a fully specified invocation, including indent-2 JSON with a trailing newline. Running the command twice over the same inputs must produce the same scorecard apart from recorded_at. The error wording is yours to choose; only the exit status, the non-empty stderr and the absent file are graded. Leave no debugging output behind.
required_outcomes: the file is runnable as a command and exits with main's return value
each of the four required flags is required, and its absence exits non-zero with stderr output
a failed invocation leaves no output file behind
the optional flags stay optional and a full invocation behaves exactly as before
nothing else in the module changes

acceptance_properties.requirement: running the command produces the scorecard
acceptance_properties.fails_when: invoking the script as a program writes no file, or its exit status is not main's return value

acceptance_properties.requirement: a wrong invocation fails instead of filing a nameless scorecard
acceptance_properties.fails_when: a missing required flag exits zero, says nothing on stderr, or leaves an output file behind
the optional flags become required, the output stops being indent-2 JSON with a trailing newline, or two identical runs differ outside recorded_at

non_goals: the six computation functions and main's aggregation, which are settled
the wording of any error message
